note: Frozen campaign config of the PAT-19 launcher (PAT-108), pinned by PAT-111 from real toy-task trials (pat-19-preflight-2026-10-05.json, then by the final trials of 2026-10-05: final cloud argv, deny-home local profile and the harness step bound, all trial-run). Changing a coordinate, a bound or a rule opens a protocol v2. A driver with verified=false is refused by a real run; verified=true needs the evidence of its trial.

bounds.note: local bounds are protocol coordinates (20 min, 40 steps); cloud_max_seconds and max_correction_rounds are operational bounds chosen by PAT-108 (protocol: 'within the limit of Foundry escalations')

isolation.note: Launcher choice, not a protocol coordinate. LOCAL drivers (sandbox-exec): reads under the user's REAL home are denied by default (deny_home_by_default, true), then only the entries of allow_read_home (relative to the home, empty by default) and the root of the harness executable's environment when it lives in the home are allowed back, plus the bundle and the attempt directory (outside the real home in a normal run); the explicit read-deny list below stays on top as a second layer (the last matching rule wins), together with every checkout/worktree of this repository, the state directory and the parent directory of --envelope/--campaign/--snapshot/--manifest (keep them apart from --work-root). Default-deny is unit-tested on the generated profile and was trial-run on 2026-10-05 with the real omp 18.6.1 and mini-swe-agent 2.4.6 (Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit, allow_read_home empty): both passed, so deny_home_by_default stays true (explicit list exercised with the real local harness by PAT-111 as well). The CLOUD drivers run WITHOUT sandbox-exec (sandbox: false with its reason) and NO read denial applies to them: neither deny_home_by_default nor the cloud list below is enforced for them (kept as data for the audit); an unsandboxed cloud arm can read anything the user can (plugin cache, ~/.config, ~/.ssh, repositories), reach the network, and use the user's implicit credentials (git credential helper through the keychain, gh configuration, ~/.config/foundry), and runs without Foundry hooks (--setting-sources project,local: the R1 guard on gh pr merge / git push does not apply). What stands between a cloud arm and the tracker, secrets and merge is: the best-effort cloud_bash_deny rules, the post-run audit of commands and paths (a record whose tool calls ran a forbidden command or touched the plugin cache, another checkout, the user's configuration, the home or an ancestor of the bundle is `contaminated`, undecided, cost kept, never replayed), and the fact that the bundle has no remote. The generated profile is itself denied to a sandboxed arm. Not covered: '(allow default)' leaves Mach access to the security daemon, so denying Library/Keychains does not prevent a keychain query.

cloud_bash_deny_note: Best-effort Bash permission rules added to --disallowedTools of the three cloud drivers (the loader refuses a real cloud driver whose argv lacks one of them). Claude Code matches a rule against the COMMAND PREFIX: they stop the direct use of the tracker, merge, network and other-agent tools (gh, git push/remote/clone/fetch/pull, curl, wget, claude, codex, omp, ssh, scp, nc, npm, pip install, python -m http, security, open). They are NOT a sandbox: a determined agent evades them (a script, an interpreter one-liner, a renamed binary, an alias, a path-qualified executable, a library call), and the cloud arm keeps the real home, an open network, the user's implicit credentials and bypassPermissions. The post-run audit (command and path audit, contaminated records) detects the direct shapes; it does not prevent anything.

min_free_disk_gib.rationale: launcher safety margin for model files and bundles; the protocol states no disk threshold

economy_time_counted.rationale: the economy verdict adds a wall-clock ratio (rules.comparison.time_ratio_max); the protocol names the premium reduction, the time ratio is the launcher's reading of 'pas trop plus de temps'

swap_metric.rationale: extra swap is measured as the maximum, over local attempts, of (swap after - swap before); the protocol does not define how to measure it

premium_work_definition.rationale: premium work = unweighted sum of the four billing token classes (input, cached input, cache write, output) over ALL models; a limit: an economy model's token weighs the same as a premium one, hence the per-model breakdown in the report, needed to judge path B honestly

economy_unavailable_when_a_compared_task.rationale: the economy verdict is `unavailable` as soon as a compared task (of the path or of A) is not decided (cap, tool failure, interruption, unreadable review) or the ledger knows of spent work the results cannot attribute; the protocol states no rule for an undecided task, this is the launcher's conservative reading (a cut path has no complete cost, comparing it would look better than what was spent)

---
Launcher note (identical for every arm): work only inside this repository. Do not create virtual environments, install packages or create node_modules in the tree; use the interpreter already on PATH. Do not create or edit test configuration files (conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, sitecustomize.py, *.pth).

prompts.implement: Implement the task described in {statement_file}. Work only inside the current repository: change the product code and add tests if useful. Run the relevant tests, then stop when you consider the task done.
prompts.correct: The task is described in {statement_file}. A previous attempt is already applied in this repository. Apply the corrections listed in {feedback_file}, run the relevant tests, then stop.
prompts.review: Independently review the uncommitted change in this repository (git diff HEAD) against the task in {statement_file}. Do not modify any file. Write {review_file} as JSON: {"verdict": "PASS" or "BLOCK", "findings": ["..."]}.

local_harness.note: Pinned on 2026-10-05 (PAT-111) from real toy-task trials of the five candidates under the launcher's local sandbox profile (protocol section 10). stdin closed, HOME isolated: the lm-studio provider is discovered from the isolated home (no home_files). --max-time 6m was accepted. The event stream has tool_execution_start events (steps) and message_end events whose assistant message carries usage (input, output, reasoningTokens).

neutral_harness.note: mini-swe-agent 2.4.6 (PyPI, isolated virtual environment, not in the repository). The executable comes from the operator variable PAT19_MINI_BIN (an absolute path whose installed package must be 2.4.6). Pinned on 2026-10-05 from a real toy-task trial under the local sandbox profile. Steps are read from the trajectory after the process ends (info.model_stats.api_calls): the launcher cannot impose the step bound while it runs, only the time bound: the harness is told its own bound (`-c agent.step_limit={max_steps}`, 40, trial-run on 2026-10-05: 8 api_calls, Submitted) and the launcher marks `step_limit_hit` a posteriori, the attempt refused, when api_calls exceeds it. LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP avoids a price-map download the sandbox blocks (about 20 s lost). OPENAI_API_KEY is a placeholder for the local server, not a secret.

session_log.layout_note: Verified on 2026-10-05 (PAT-111): the launcher's reading of <projects_dir>/*/<session>.jsonl equals the host's own result.usage exactly for the three drivers, one file per session id. Conditional on the launcher's assertion, from the stream's system/init event, that the arm's tools are a subset of allowed_tools (Bash, Edit, Read, Write; so no sub-agent, workflow, web or scheduling tool): a record whose init event lists any other tool, or has none, is refused (tool_error).

cloud_implementer_current.note: Claude Code 2.1.285 headless, current routed implementer profile (Sonnet 5.5, effort medium). The first 2026-10-05 trial ran with `--disallowedTools Agent` only; the FINAL argv (29 tool names + the cloud_bash_deny rules) was then trial-run on the toy task on 2026-10-05 (init: exactly Bash, Edit, Read, Write) and passed, see the evidence. Bare Claude Code with the protocol's model and effort: no Foundry plugin, hook, agent definition (not the Eiffel or Maigret definitions), --permission-mode bypassPermissions, tools restricted to Read/Edit/Write/Bash with Bash otherwise unrestricted except for the best-effort deny rules.
cloud_implementer_current.sandbox_reason: Claude Code cannot authenticate under sandbox-exec ('Not logged in' with the keychain denied, '401 OAuth access token has been revoked' with it allowed; cause not established). The arm runs unsandboxed with the AGENTS.md R6 environment intact (real HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TMPDIR, USER) in the disposable bundle; its tool calls are audited after the run. Consequences, not mitigated by the launcher: real home, open network, the user's implicit credentials, no Foundry hook (no R1 guard); see cloud_bash_deny and isolation.note.

candidates_note: model = the LM Studio model key, which is also the identifier the operator gives at load (lms load <key> -c 65536 --identifier <key> --parallel 1) and the name the harness sends; the HF repo of the protocol is kept as hf_repo_provenance. The operator loads, the launcher loads nothing. The preflight reads the loaded instance (lms ps --json) and refuses when its model key differs, its quantization differs or its context length is below min_context (65536, a frozen coordinate: LM Studio ignored -c for some MLX builds). File digests, chat-template digest and generation parameters are recorded here and in pat-19-preflight-2026-10-05.json; they are not recomputed by the launcher. Generation parameters are the server and harness defaults, not overridden.
